scope: Selected throwaway Desk prototype only; no redesign and no production UNIT changes.

scriptedChecks.clippedTextFinding: The only reported node is the intentional .np-visually-hidden Editorial Columns heading; no visible text is clipped.

firstViewport.finding: UNIT is the clear departure subject, then the folded newspaper becomes the first Desk focal point with the next scene kept below the opening ritual.

signatureInteraction.finding: The screenshots show a legible UNIT plate exit, fully opaque Paper Bridge, covered swap, folded Desk handoff, scroll opening, ink resolution and committed masthead stamp.

bridgeAndHandoff.finding: Both desktop and mobile covered-swap frames are opaque edge to edge. The handoff keeps paper color, crease, pose and shadow coherent without a visible mixed-layout frame.

sectionEventUniqueness.finding: Lead places a taped clipping; Columns deals a reading pile and opens a diary; Classified pulls torn paper and stamps VACANT; About opens the owner's book and deals labels; Index opens a ruled notebook; Exchange deals and postmarks postcards; Outro folds and feeds the edition into the mail slot.

motionLanguage.finding: Paper folds, crease shadows, wet ink, tape pressure, stamps, dealt desk objects and mail-slot delivery form one consistent physical language.

scrollNarrative.finding: One edition moves from print-plate departure through arrival and opening, across a working desk's reading and filing actions, then ends as a delivered folded paper.

mobile.finding: No incoherent overlap or visible text obstruction is present. Lead, Classified, About and Index stay in document flow; Columns and Exchange preserve contained horizontal strips with a clear next-item hint.

reducedMotion.finding: The live preference change reaches the complete static Desk in 43.6ms with zero active animations; the opening distance collapses and the newspaper remains readable.

remainingDeviations.deviation: All chapter observers commit through the shared is-in-view class instead of one event-specific completed class and a completedEvents record.
remainingDeviations.risk: The physical effects are visually distinct, but production analytics, replay policy or per-event lifecycle changes would be harder to isolate.

remainingDeviations.deviation: The covered swap relies on the fixed bridge geometry and scheduled phase timing rather than a runtime bounding-rect and computed-opacity assertion before layoutSwapped changes.
remainingDeviations.risk: Current desktop/mobile measurements pass; add the runtime assertion only when this throwaway prototype is ported to production or its geometry becomes dynamic.

remainingDeviations.deviation: Wheel, touchstart or Escape acceleration calls finishTransition directly instead of visibly snapping through bridge coverage and the frame-matched handoff.
remainingDeviations.risk: This intentionally prioritizes a stable state under interruption and settles in 2.2ms, well below the 100ms contract; the accelerated path does not preserve the full visual continuity of the normal path.

remainingDeviations.deviation: Outro folding is a one-shot IntersectionObserver event rather than the specified scroll-linked fold progress with a .92 delivery commit.
remainingDeviations.risk: The final delivery beat is visually complete, but production should tighten it if reversible, progress-coupled folding remains a requirement.

finalGate.finding: Heavy visual acceptance passes at 90/100 with no hard fails. The core interaction, narrative motion, mobile layout and reduced-motion behavior are complete; listed implementation-contract deviations remain non-blocking for this throwaway prototype.
